note: The 'three big girl groups' member — comeback drought or not, still a top pick.
bio: South Korean girl group formed by YG Entertainment, debuting August 8, 2016 with Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé, and Lisa. One of K-pop's biggest global acts, known for long gaps between releases and huge individual solo careers. Fandom name BLINK is a portmanteau of 'Black' and 'Pink,' officially confirmed in early 2017.

note: Empowering-anthem energy since debut, no filler eras.
bio: South Korean girl group under JYP Entertainment, debuting February 12, 2019 with 'DALLA DALLA.' Members: Yeji, Lia, Ryujin, Chaeryeong, Yuna. Fandom name MIDZY (믿지) means 'trust' in Korean, reflecting a mutual-trust relationship between group and fans, announced July 8, 2019.

note: Fresh debut, already deserves a permanent slot.
bio: Eight-member project group formed through SBS survival show 'Universe Ticket,' with Korean, Japanese, and Filipino members (Hyeonju, Yunha, Yoona, Seowon, Nana, Kotoko, Gehlee, Elisia). Debuted with 'SUPERWOMAN.' Fandom name EverAfter was announced May 15, drawn from 'happily ever after.'

note: YG's newest generation, already hitting hard.
bio: Seven-member South Korean girl group under YG Entertainment (Ruka, Pharita, Asa, Ahyeon, Rami, Rora, Chiquita). Debuted as six members Nov 27, 2023 with 'Batter Up,' completed to seven with the April 1, 2024 mini album 'BABYMONS7ER.' Fandom name MONSTIEZ, revealed July 27, 2024, combines 'MONS' with 'ties.'

note: The Philippines' own — 'nation's girl group' isn't an exaggeration.
bio: Eight-member Filipino girl group (Aiah, Colet, Maloi, Gwen, Stacey, Mikha, Jhoanna, Sheena) under Star Music/ABS-CBN, debuting in 2021. Widely dubbed the 'National Girl Group of the Philippines,' first P-pop act at Coachella, and joined Weverse in March 2026. Fandom name: Blooms.

note: Kings of P-pop, and they've earned the title.
bio: Five-member Filipino boy group (Pablo, Stell, Ken, Josh, Justin) formed via ShowBT Philippines, debuting in 2018. Known as the 'Kings of P-pop,' first Filipino act on Billboard's Next Big Sound chart, joined Weverse March 2026. Fandom name A'TIN (pronounced 'eighteen') also reads as the Filipino word for 'ours.'

note: Bubblegum pop hooks with a HUNTR/X-level cover to prove the vocals.
bio: Five-member Filipino girl group under ShowBT Philippines/Sony Music PH (Angela, Charice, Alexa, Sophia, Charlotte), officially debuting April 8, 2022. Name comes from the Cebuano word 'kinaiya' (inner character/individuality). Fandom name: ZAIA, official colors cyan and magenta.

note: 'P-pop's Female Alphas,' girl-crush concept done right.
bio: Filipino girl group under Cornerstone Entertainment, launched 2022, currently three members (AJ, Alfea, Jaz). Group name references the Glock 22 (tied to debut single 'Bang!'), giving rise to the fandom name Bullets. Dubbed 'P-pop's Female Alphas'; debut album 'The Dissection of Eve' released November 2025.

note: Sings in seven Philippine regional languages — cultural pride as concept.
bio: Filipino boy group under Viva, debuting February 14, 2021 with 'Kbye.' Distinct for singing in seven Philippine languages (Bikolano, Cebuano, Hiligaynon, Ilocano, Kapampangan, Tagalog, Waray-Waray). Second P-pop act on Billboard's Next Big Sound chart after SB19; set to perform in Paris in October 2026. Fandom name Magiliw means 'affectionate' in Tagalog.

note: 'Asia's Phoenix' — the riffs alone are a whole personality.
bio: Johanne Morissette Daug Amon, Filipino singer-songwriter from Cebu, active since 2010. Rose to fame on 'The Voice of the Philippines' (2013) and earned the nickname 'Asia's Phoenix' after her 2017 Asia Song Festival performance in Busan. No official coined fandom name — she's a solo act, not an idol group.

note: Screams the heartbreak instead of just singing it — the Wish Bus clips prove it.
bio: Patricia Janine Dusaran Berdin, Filipino singer-songwriter from Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu. Won Tawag ng Tanghalan Season 2 in 2018 at age 16. Her 2022 duet 'Mahika' (with Adie) became the longest-charting track in Billboard Philippines Songs chart history. No official fandom name — solo artist.

note: Went from rejected audition tapes to a sold-out two-night Frontier Theater run.
bio: Ralph William Datoon, Filipino R&B/alternative singer-songwriter from Quezon City, signed to Tarsier Records since 2021. Broke out with 'Saan?' and 'Bakit?' (2023 EP 'Tanong'), then hit mainstream with 'Dilaw' (2024), one of the few Filipino songs to chart globally on Spotify. Debut album 'Kolorcoaster' released September 2025. No official fandom name — solo artist.
